newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ civil defence issues storm warning.
newsitem.headline: NZ civil defence issues storm warning.

text.p: New Zealand's director of civil defence warned holidaymakers on Thursday to beware of high winds and heavy rainfall from approaching Cyclone Drena.

"As this is still the peak holiday season, all holidaymakers, campers, trampers, potholers and people engaged in sea and freshwater leisure pursuits, air-related leisure activities, and road users are further reminded of the significant dangers that high winds and heavy rainfall can bring," a civil defence statement said.
Director Paul Officer said disruption was possible to air and road travel, and people should consult the airlines and Automobile Association or Transit New Zealand.
"The public are advised to listen to their local radio stations and heed the advice of tier local civil defence or emergency management organisations," he said.
Emergency services would be "busy enough" and people should not engage in hazardous activities that would stretch them even further, Officer said.
A MetService special weather bulletin forecast up to 21 hours of heavy rain and periods of damaging winds.

Chief meteorologist Augie Auer earlier advised campers in the north of the country to pack up and leave, saying Drena would be even more severe than the remnants of Cyclone Fergus, which hit New Zealand shortly before the New Year.
Auer said the cyclone was expected to track down the west side of the North Island. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
